As of 315 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Much cooler with rain today. Gusty winds/breezy 
conditions are expected, especially along the immediate coast.

Early this morning, a potent cold front has dropped south through a 
majority of the forecast area (currently located just north of the 
Albemarle Sound). In the wake of the front, winds have turned to the 
N-NW and widespread rain is beginning to develop. Temperatures have 
dropped into the 50s for N/NW portions of the forecast area as 
cooler air continues to filter into the area. 

The front clears the local area completely over the next few hours, 
but an overrunning/anafrontal setup is expected with light to 
moderate rain continuing into the late morning-early afternoon 
inland and for much of the day across the SE. High temperatures have 
likely already been achieved at most locations today, with 
widespread cloud cover and rain holding temperatures in the low to 
mid 50s this afternoon. Gradual clearing is expected from the NW by 
late morning, with some sunshine possible for areas along and west 
of I-95 later this afternoon into the evening. 

Along the immediate coast, and especially Virginia Beach and 
Currituck County, the tightening pressure gradient between high 
pressure to our northwest and developing low pressure offshore will 
allow northerly winds to increase to 25 to 30 mph with gusts up to 
45 to 50 mph this afternoon. Wind Advisories remain in effect for 
Virginia Beach and Currituck starting at noon today.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Patchy frost is possible Sunday morning across the 
Piedmont. Much cooler on Sunday. 

Any steady rain moves offshore this evening, with clearing 
continuing from NW to SE across the local area. Strong, 1030+ mb, 
high pressure building in from our west will allow for much drier 
and chilly air to filter into the local area tonight. Lows will drop 
back into the mid 30s (and potentially some lower 30s) in the 
typically colder, sheltered rural Piedmont locations, upper 30s 
along I-95, and mid 40s to mid 50s along the coast. While some 
patchy frost is possible early Sunday morning in the typically 
cooler and sheltered Piedmont locations, a persistent 5 to 10 mph 
northerly breeze will prevent widespread decoupling. Therefore, no 
frost headlines are in effect locally at this time. Sunday will be 
noticeably cooler/fall-like with high temperatures only ranging from 
the upper 50s to lower 60s. Skies will be partly to mostly sunny, 
with some stratocumulus likely lingering across our far SE areas. 
Another patchy frost potential is possible for far NW Piedmont 
locations Sunday night-early Monday AM. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...There is still some uncertainty for next week with a 
Nor'easter lingering offshore or retrograding back towards the local 
area.

There is still a decent amount of uncertainty with respect to the 
track and strength of a nor'easter late this weekend into early next 
week. Guidance continues to struggle with how close this system 
remains to the shoreline, though most of the ensemble solutions show 
the low meandering around 100-200 miles off the southern VA or NC 
coast. It should also be noted that much of the 00z guidance has 
shifted the system further offshore compared to the 12z suite. 
Regardless of the exact center position, high confidence exists in a 
multi-day period of strong onshore winds, high surf, and coastal 
flooding through at least midweek. Rain chances remain highest (30-
50% PoP) across eastern portions of the area, with dry conditions 
inland. Temperatures this week will generally be running near to 
slightly below normal with daytime highs in the 60s and lows in the 
40s inland to 50s at the coast.


KEY MESSAGE 4...Long Duration coastal flood event expected 
starting as early as Sunday afternoon, but potentially 
continuing into mid week. Coastal flood watches issued for the 
Lower Chesapeake Bay and Lower James River with expansion of 
coastal flood watches likely to other areas tonight or Saturday.

North winds to gale force will allow water levels to build first 
over the lower Bay and Lower James River as early as Sunday 
afternoon. This will allow for tide anomalies to be 2 to 3 feet 
above normal astronomical tide. Fortunately, we are currently on the 
low end of the tide cycle. Even so, moderate flood stage is forecast 
at Lynnhaven, Jamestown and Smithfield with the Sunday high tide. As 
the winds turn slightly more northeast and increase Sunday night 
into Monday, expect the anomalies to build and impact the ocean 
front, as well as other areas in the lower and middle Chesapeake 
Bay. By Monday, many sites south of Windmill Point and along the 
ocean front are forecast to be into moderate flooding, including 
Sewells Pt. Lynnhaven, Jamestown and Smithfield are forecast to 
major tidal flooding on Monday. Considerable beach erosion is also 
expected with seas building to 10 to 15 feet. With little change in
